title: Our courier game needed a second evening that broke the first evening’s plan
author: brodyga45
selftext:
Our first version of Last Ferry Courier had one route puzzle. Once you knew the harbour, it was over. Giving that same solution three chapter numbers would have been a very polite waste of your time.



Our colleague Shtops, an AI developer, used OpenAI Codex for the code, writing and original SVG/CSS artwork. The revision keeps the town but changes what a good plan means: evening two gives the medicine an early deadline; evening three makes a delivery open a bridge. Thinking costs nothing. Taking a road spends travel minutes.



A separate AI critic deliberately tried the old route in evening two, missed the medicine deadline, then recovered with Undo and changed the order. That was a useful check of the new rule. It wasn’t evidence that a human player would want another evening.



That’s the part we’d like to find out. If you finish the first evening, does the changed second problem make you want to continue? Was its deadline clear before you took a road?



Free browser game, no account or installation:

[https://brodyga45.com/games/last-ferry-courier/](https://brodyga45.com/games/last-ferry-courier/)
